description.before: Illustrative grid-frequency experiment with physically consistent rotating-energy balance. Power is MW, time seconds, frequency Hz and kinetic energy MW s. Initial stored energy is derived from the existing System Inertia (5 s) times Base Generation (1000 MW), rather than an independent inconsistent 100. The net Inertial Response is demand minus generation, allowing both kinetic discharge and recharge. Frequency Change follows the exact nonlinear swing-energy identity df/dt=(Pgen-Pload)*f/(2E), retaining E/(f/f0)^2=5000 MW s. Adaptive Radau preserves the kinetic invariant to relative error below 2e-11 over the full 60 s, keeps the original output step .01, and permits half/quarter output refinements within the work budget. All original elements, geometry, forcing, droop and reserve paths remain. Governor/droop/reserve dynamics are illustrative local assumptions; this is not a reproduction of the NREL virtual-synchronous-generator network.
description.after: Illustrative grid-frequency experiment with physically consistent rotating-energy balance. Power is MW, time seconds, frequency Hz and kinetic energy MW s. Initial stored energy is System Inertia (5 s) times Base Generation (1000 MW). Net Inertial Response is demand minus generation, permitting kinetic discharge and recharge. Frequency Change follows df/dt=(Pgen-Pload)*f/(2E), preserving E/(f/f0)^2=5000 MW s. Explicit RK4 at DT 0.04 s handles the illustrative reserve deadband without claiming adaptive event localization; full 60 s default, half and quarter grids fit the engine work budget. The frequency-energy invariant agrees with the independent reduced swing equation near floating-point precision; reserve relative error is below 1e-7 against an event-split reference. All original forcing, droop and reserve paths remain. Governor/droop/reserve dynamics are illustrative local assumptions; this is not a reproduction of the NREL virtual-synchronous-generator network.

description.after: Illustrative traffic stock-flow model using a linear speed-density relation and queue heuristics. Lighthill and Whitham (1955), Part II, is conceptual background; this file is not a verified spatial discretization or reproduction of the LWR conservation law. description.before: Stanley Milgram's 1967 'six degrees of separation' experiment showing social networks have small average path lengths despite large size. Reference: Milgram, S. (1967). The Small World Problem. Psychology Today, 2(1), 60-67. Source: https://doi.org/10.1037/e400002009-005
description.after: Illustrative continuous logistic network-reach experiment, conceptually associated with Milgram small-world studies. This generated logistic ODE is not a reconstruction of the 1967 acquaintance-chain experiment. People_Reached obeys dP/dt=50*P*(1-P/300000000). The legacy Chain_Steps stock integrates elapsed model time while reach is below half the population; it is not a count of discrete acquaintance links. Avg_Path_Length and Steps_Remaining are retained heuristic logarithmic quantities. Explicit RK4 DT 0.0025 resolves the logistic transition over the unchanged full 10-unit horizon. Default/half/quarter grids fit the work budget and agree with the exact logistic solution; threshold-duration error is bounded by half a timestep, with nonmonotone grid-phase error. No empirical calibration or native Milgram simulation is claimed.

description.before: Jay Forrester’s five-sector WORLD2 global dynamics model. Version 1.8 restores the 1970 primary D-1354 documentor (MIT archive PDF pp. 82–91), including its 22 piecewise-linear feedback tables, birth/death normals 0.045/0.025 and initial agricultural fraction 0.3. Existing element IDs and positions are preserved. Capital Generation Multiplier is the source CIPC table divided by the retained 0.05 normal, an algebraically identical rescaling. The documented baseline pre/post-1970 policy coefficients are equal. Explicit Radau integration preserves the 1900–2100 annual output grid. This historical scenario is not a contemporary population or climate calibration.
